A1.justification: Despite the changed title and formatting, both PDFs describe the same functional-head identification and rescaling work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons on three model backbones, head-rescaling ablations, sensitivity experiments, inference timings, and qualitative case analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original results on five benchmarks and the appendix case studies, and additionally reports a manual breakdown of 200 hallucination cases and an Ocean-R1 efficiency plot.

M1.justification: The stated head-selection statistic changes from averaging attention over all query positions in v1 Equation (4) to using one query position i* in v2 Equation (7). However, v2's prose and Figure 2 still specify averaging, so an implemented procedural change is unresolved. The head categories and output-rescaling mechanism otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 removes quantitative CLEVR evaluation from Tables 1, 2, and 4 and its dataset description, narrowing synthetic compositional-VQA evaluation. The other five benchmarks and three task domains remain. Appendix H.5 retains the synthetic-object qualitative example, so this scenario is not entirely removed.

E2.justification: Vanilla, VCD, CGD, and AGLA remain the comparators in the retained benchmark and runtime comparisons. The added Ocean-R1 efficiency panel uses the same comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 Section 2.3 introduces manual classification of a sample of 200 hallucination cases, adding an evaluation procedure and sample size. Case selection and annotation procedures are unspecified. The retained benchmark metrics, backbones, hardware settings, and Table 5 hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a quantitative error-type breakdown from 200 cases. Figure 4 replaces the CLEVR boundary-sensitivity analysis with HallusionBench, and Table 2 removes CLEVR ablations. The remaining component ablations, gain/threshold sensitivity analyses, and all four Appendix H case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain the same value-plus/minus reporting, including identical uncertainty values for retained entries. Neither version explains run counts, seeds, or the meaning of those uncertainty terms; v2 introduces no confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: All retained entries in Tables 1, 2, and 4 are identical; CLEVR entries are removed. The reported average accuracy gain changes from 4.8 to 4.2 points with the narrower benchmark mix, not from improved scores. New results include the 16% perceptual-bias, 20% reasoning-drift, and 10% co-occurrence figures, the Ocean-R1 efficiency panel, and a HallusionBench boundary sweep peaking at 53.64%, replacing the different-task CLEVR sweep peaking at 43.37%.

T1.justification: v2 adds squared-distance definitions of perceptual and reasoning deviation, a weighted hallucination-intensity quantity, and a minimal-intervention optimization formulation in Sections 2.3–3. It also revises the attention-ratio definition. These are limited formal additions; the existing Appendix B proofs and Appendix C complexity derivations remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The training-free, two-stage contribution is retained. v1's abstract claims 5% average and up to 15% improvement; v2 reports a 4.2-percentage-point average, with up to 7% stated in the introduction. v2 also removes the claims of complete model agnosticism and enabling safe high-stakes deployment, narrowing its applicability claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets hallucination through deviations from ideal representations and asserts that rescaling reduces these deviations 'by construction.' It adds an interpretation that hyperparameters operate stably over a broad region and changes the visual-task reasoning-layer interpretation from approximately layer 9 onward to layer 5 onward. The substantive appendix limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes the code-access statement and link supplied in v1's abstract. It also removes the explicit statement that ablations keep all other hyperparameters identical. Hardware disclosures, implementation function/file names, caching information, and Table 5 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The CLEVR paper by Johnson et al. is removed from the citations and bibliography. The remaining related-work coverage and positioning are essentially preserved. v2's abstract more explicitly attributes staged attention allocation to prior interpretability findings, already discussed in v1's main text.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, rewrites the abstract and localized motivation/method passages, introduces an Experimental Setup subsection, and shortens the conclusion. It removes the LLM language-editing disclosure. Most narrative text and the main-section and appendix ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. Appendix tables and case-study boxes are reflowed, including consolidating Table 3 onto one page. Tables 1, 2, and 4 lose CLEVR columns; Figure 3 gains an Ocean-R1 panel, and Figure 4 replaces its middle panel and revises axis labeling.

improvement.justification: v2 makes headline gains consistent with the retained Table 1 results and removes overbroad deployment claims, while adding limited diagnostic evidence. However, it removes quantitative CLEVR evidence and the code-access link, introduces a head-selection equation that conflicts with retained averaging descriptions, and asserts reduction of a new hallucination quantity without establishing it through proof or measurement. These benefits and harms leave the net quality direction uncertain.
